findings.title: Access-token id matcher is inverted and slices the wrong characters
findings.body: isAccessTokenId is what expectRefresh, expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, and expectAuthReqIdToToken use to check the new jti format. matchesSafely returns false when items[0].substring(3, 5) equals the expected grant shortcut, so a correct shortcut is treated as a mismatch. The slice is also wrong: the prefix is session (2) + token type (2) + grant (2), so the grant shortcut is substring(4, 6), not substring(3, 5). A default regular refresh token id is like onrtrt:<uuid>; substring(3, 5) is rt, which equals RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT, so expectRefresh fails on a correctly encoded token. For authorization-code (ac), device (dg), and CIBA (ci) the wrong slice does not equal the shortcut, so the inverted check never fires and those assertions pass even if the grant shortcut is wrong, as long as the suffix looks like a UUID. If the prefix is shorter than 5 characters, substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of failing the assertion.

findings.title: Null raw token id is not rejected
findings.body: The AccessTokenContext constructor is meant to reject a null raw token id, but the fourth requireNonNull checks grantType again (the message says "Null rawTokenId not allowed") and never reads rawTokenId. A null raw id is stored. encodeTokenId concatenates it with ':', and Java string conversion turns that null into the literal characters null, so the jti becomes something like onrtac:null. Those ids are not unique and will not round-trip to a real token id. The check must be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are registered without length or uniqueness checks
findings.body: postInit and getShortcutByGrantType (around line 113) register shortcuts with an unconditional Map.put. A shortcut that is already mapped is overwritten, so decoding that two-character code returns the newly registered grant and previously issued access tokens are classified as the wrong grant. The size comparison that is supposed to catch duplicate ids or shortcuts runs only at the end of postInit; the hot-deploy path that reloads a newly deployed grant does not repeat it. Shortcuts are also not required to be exactly two characters, which getTokenContextFromTokenId assumes (6-character prefix, three slices of 2). A shortcut of any other length, including the 3-letter form described on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut, is stored and encodeTokenId will emit it, but decoding that jti throws IllegalArgumentException. A null shortcut NPEs inside ConcurrentHashMap.put and can abort startup or token issuance. Registration should reject null, non-length-2, and duplicate shortcuts instead of overwriting.

findings.title: getShortcut() is a new abstract SPI method with no default
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() was added with no default implementation. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls it on every OAuth2GrantType factory. An existing custom grant-type factory compiled against the previous SPI will throw AbstractMethodError during that call and prevent the server from starting, and will not compile against this interface until it is updated. A default that returns a reserved unknown shortcut (or skipping factories that cannot provide one) would keep old providers from taking down startup. The new javadoc on line 30 also says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but the encoder only accepts exactly two characters and will not successfully decode anything else.
